summary: Complete target-level plan of all six layers of the Part II. VS6 defines decent v-stacks and fine morphisms after Gulotta–Hansen–Weinstein, with classifying stacks, 2-morphisms and the representability of proper fine maps. VS7 constructs the exceptional functors for fine maps (prespatial diamonds, the enhanced operation map on qcqs v-sheaves, DESCENT to decent v-stacks), the six-functor identities, the proper comparison, intrinsic smoothness and relative dualizing complexes. VS8 identifies sheaves on constant locally profinite diamonds and on classifying stacks with smooth modules and representations, with all four operations and Haar-measure twists. VS9 plans the generic trace formalism of Lu–Zheng, D(Λ)-dualizability, the 2-categories Corr_S and CoCorr_S, dualizability as ULA-ness, trace classes and characteristic classes. VS10 proves the relative Lefschetz–Verdier trace formula, proper pushforward of characteristic classes, the Lefschetz formula for proper diamonds, local terms and their base change and perfect-scheme comparison. VS11 treats admissible objects and trace distributions on classifying stacks, the Künneth formula through based cohomological correspondences, and universal local terms for group actions. Two gaps remain (Liu–Zheng DESCENT has no owner; an exercise of Gulotta–Hansen–Weinstein), and the plan corrects one stated remark of Hansen–Kaletha–Weinstein (étaleness of inertia at isolated fixed points).

nodes.title: Maps representable in locally separated locally spatial diamonds
nodes.statement: A locally spatial diamond is locally separated if it has an open cover by separated locally spatial diamonds. A map f : X → Y of small v-stacks is representable in locally separated locally spatial diamonds if for every locally separated locally spatial diamond T with a map T → Y the fibre product X ×_Y T is a locally separated locally spatial diamond. It suffices to test separated spatial diamonds T. Such maps are representable in diamonds; the class is stable under composition and base change; quasicompact injections belong to it; and if g ∘ f belongs to it with g 0-truncated and quasiseparated, then f belongs to it.
hypotheses: X, Y are small v-stacks.
Everything lives over the category Perf of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with its v-topology.
proofSteps: Reduce the test objects to separated spatial T: a locally separated locally spatial T is covered by separated spatial opens, and both properties of the fibre product are local on T (GHW22 remark after Definition 4.1).
Representability in diamonds: test against affinoid perfectoid T, which are separated spatial diamonds, so X ×_Y T is a diamond (GHW22 Proposition 4.3(i), first claim).
Composition and base change are formal from the definition (GHW22 Proposition 4.3(ii)).

Quasicompact injections into a locally spatial diamond have locally spatial source (Sch17 Proposition 11.20, recorded by DiamondsAndVStacks D5); separatedness passes to subobjects (GHW22 Proposition 4.3(iii)).
For g 0-truncated and quasiseparated, X ×_Y T → X ×_Z T is a base change of the quasicompact injection Y → Y ×_Z Y, so the previous step applies (GHW22 Proposition 4.3(iv)).
acceptance: The identity of every small v-stack has the property; an open immersion of locally spatial diamonds has it.
The structure map [S/G_S] → S of a classifying stack of a nontrivial locally profinite group does not have it: its fibres are stacks with nontrivial automorphism groups.

nodes.title: Decent v-stacks
nodes.statement: A small v-stack X is decent if (1) its diagonal X → X × X is representable in locally separated locally spatial diamonds, and (2) there is a locally separated locally spatial diamond U and a surjective map U → X that is representable in locally spatial diamonds and, locally on U, separated and cohomologically smooth (ℓ-cohomologically smooth for every prime ℓ ≠ p). Such U → X is a chart; it is a clean chart if U is separated and U → X is separated and cohomologically smooth, and every decent v-stack has a clean chart. For locally separated locally spatial diamonds T → X ← T′ the fibre product T ×_X T′ is a locally separated locally spatial diamond.
hypotheses: X is a small v-stack.
Everything lives over the category Perf of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with its v-topology.
Cohomological smoothness is that of DiamondSixOperations S4 for maps representable in locally spatial diamonds.
proofSteps: Clean charts: refine U by an open cover by separated spatial pieces on which the chart is separated and smooth and take the disjoint union (GHW22 Remark 1.2(ii)).
Fibre products of test diamonds: T ×_X T′ = (T × T′) ×_{X×X} X, and T × T′ is a locally separated locally spatial diamond (GHW22 Remark 1.2(i)).

Hansen–Kaletha–Weinstein's restatement (HKW22 Definition 4.1.7) asks for a strictly surjective chart that is locally compactifiable of finite dim.trg; the plan uses the public GHW22 Definition 1.1 and records the difference in sourceIssues.
acceptance: Every locally separated locally spatial diamond is decent, with the identity as chart.
Spd Z_p and Div¹ are decent but not diamonds (VS6/decent-v-stack-examples).
For G closed in GL_n(E) the classifying stack [S/G_S] is decent with chart GL_n^♢ × S / G_S, while the point map S → [S/G_S] is not a chart when G has an infinite compact open subgroup.

nodes.title: Fibre products of decent v-stacks
nodes.statement: If X₂ → X₁ ← X₃ are maps of decent v-stacks, then X₂ ×_{X₁} X₃ is decent; in particular absolute products of decent v-stacks are decent. If U_i → X_i are charts, U₂ ×_{X₁} U₃ → X₂ ×_{X₁} X₃ is a chart.
hypotheses: X₁, X₂, X₃ are decent v-stacks with maps X₂ → X₁ ← X₃.
proofSteps: Charts: U₂ ×_{X₁} U₃ is a locally separated locally spatial diamond by decency of X₁ (VS6/decent-v-stack), and U₂ ×_{X₁} U₃ → X₂ ×_{X₁} X₃ factors as two base changes of charts, hence is a chart (DiamondSixOperations S4 smoothness stable under base change and composition).
Diagonal: the map u : X₂ ×_{X₁} X₃ → X₂ × X₃ is a base change of the diagonal of X₁, hence representable in locally separated locally spatial diamonds and quasiseparated (VS6/decent-is-artin).

The composite of the diagonal of the fibre product with u × u equals the diagonal of X₂ × X₃ composed with u; cancel u × u, which is 0-truncated and quasiseparated, using the cancellation property of VS6/locally-separated-representability (GHW22 Proposition 4.5).
acceptance: For decent S, products X ×_S Y of decent S-v-stacks are decent, as the tensor product of Corr_S requires.
The inertia stack In_S(X) = X ×_{X ×_S X} X of a decent X is decent.

nodes.title: Fine morphisms of decent v-stacks
nodes.statement: A map f : X → Y of decent v-stacks is fine if there is a commutative square with charts a : V → Y and b : W → X and a map g : W → V that is, locally on W, compactifiable of finite dim.trg. Equivalently, there is such a square with clean charts and g compactifiable of locally finite dim.trg; equivalently, with V → Y a chart, U = X ×_Y V and a chart W′ → U such that W′ → V is locally compactifiable of finite dim.trg. For every square of charts over a fine f the top map is locally compactifiable of finite dim.trg.
hypotheses: X, Y are decent v-stacks.
proofSteps: Clean form: refine V and W as in VS6/decent-v-stack and use Sch17 Proposition 22.3 to pass compactifiability through separated local isomorphisms (GHW22 Remark 4.6).

Cartesian form: given a square, set U = X ×_Y V and W′ = W ×_Y V; decency of Y makes W′ a locally separated locally spatial diamond and W′ → U a chart; W′ → V is a base change of f ∘ b (GHW22 Remark 4.7).
Independence of charts: compare two squares through W ×_X W′ using Sch17 Proposition 22.3(ii),(iv),(vii),(viii) and universal openness of smooth charts (GHW22 Proposition 4.8(o)).
acceptance: Every map of decent v-stacks that is representable in locally spatial diamonds, compactifiable and locally of finite dim.trg is fine.
The structure map [S/G_S] → S of HKW22 Example 4.2.4 is fine and not representable.

nodes.title: Permanence of fine morphisms
nodes.statement: (i) Fine maps are stable under composition. (ii) Base changes of fine maps along maps of decent v-stacks are fine. (iii) If h : X → Z and g : Y → Z are fine, every map f : X → Y with g ∘ f = h is fine. (iv) A separated map of decent v-stacks representable in locally spatial diamonds is fine iff it is compactifiable of locally finite dim.trg. In particular, for a correspondence X ← C → X′ of decent S-v-stacks with C → X′ fine and X, X′ fine over S, both legs and C → S are fine.
hypotheses: All v-stacks are decent.

nodes.title: Classifying stacks of group diamonds and their 2-morphisms
nodes.statement: For a diamond S and a group diamond G → S, BG = [S/G] is the small v-stack of right G-torsors, with S ×_{BG} S ≅ G. For group diamonds G, H over S, the groupoid of S-maps BG → BH is equivalent to the groupoid of right H-torsors P on S with a commuting left G-action (equivalently homomorphisms G → Aut_H(P)), with equivariant torsor isomorphisms as arrows; the map sends Q to Q ×^G P. A homomorphism f : G → H induces φ_f : BG → BH (P the trivial torsor), and 2-morphisms φ_{f₁} ⇒ φ_{f₂} are the h ∈ H(S) with f₁ = ad(h) ∘ f₂. For G acting on a diamond X over S, [X/G] is the quotient stack. In the notation [T_S/G_S] for a locally profinite set T with an action of a locally profinite group G, T_S and G_S are the constant diamonds over S.
hypotheses: S is a diamond; G, H are group diamonds over S.
This corrects HKW22 Example 4.1.1, which identifies all maps BG → BH with homomorphisms (sourceIssues).
proofSteps: Torsor description: an S-map BG → BH is determined by the image P of the trivial G-torsor, an H-torsor with a commuting G-action given by the automorphisms of the trivial G-torsor (descent along S → BG, DiamondsAndVStacks D4 small v-stacks).
A chosen trivialisation P ≅ H turns the G-action into a homomorphism G → H; changing the trivialisation conjugates it.
For maps induced by specified homomorphisms, a 2-morphism is an H-equivariant automorphism of the trivial torsor intertwining the actions, i.e. left multiplication by h ∈ H(S) with f₁ = ad(h) ∘ f₂.
acceptance: For S = Spd Q_p, G = 1 and H the constant group Z/2, the unramified quadratic extension gives a map B1 = S → BH not induced by a homomorphism 1 → H.

For S = Spd C (C algebraically closed) and constant locally profinite G, H, every H-torsor on S is trivial and Hom_S(BG, BH) is the groupoid of continuous homomorphisms G → H with conjugation by H as arrows.

nodes.title: Compatibility of pullback and pushforward with 2-morphisms
nodes.statement: For maps f, g : Y → X of small v-stacks and a 2-morphism α : f ⇒ g there are natural isomorphisms α^* : f^* ≅ g^* and α_* : Rf_* ≅ Rg_* such that α_* α^* carries the unit id → Rf_* f^* to the unit id → Rg_* g^* and the counit f^* Rf_* → id to the counit g^* Rg_* → id; these isomorphisms are compatible with vertical and horizontal composition of 2-morphisms.
hypotheses: X, Y are small v-stacks; Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: D_ét(−, Λ) is a v-sheaf of ∞-categories on small v-stacks (Sch17 §17, recorded in DiamondEtaleCohomology and EnhancedDerivedSheaves E2), so f ↦ f^* is a pseudo-functor out of the (2,1)-category of small v-stacks; α^* is its value on α.
α_* is the mate of (α^{-1})^* under the adjunctions f^* ⊣ Rf_*, g^* ⊣ Rg_*; the two stated diagrams are the defining identities of a mate (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E3/mates-and-beck-chevalley).

nodes.title: Proper nice maps of decent v-stacks
nodes.statement: A map of small v-stacks is proper if it is quasicompact, separated and universally closed (Sch17 Definition 18.1); separated maps of v-stacks have closed immersions, hence injections, as diagonals, so proper maps are 0-truncated. A map f : X → Y of decent v-stacks is proper nice if it is proper, representable in locally spatial diamonds and locally of finite dim.trg. Proper nice maps are fine, stable under composition and base change, and their exceptional pushforward in the sense of DiamondSixOperations S2 is defined and equals Rf_*. Throughout this roadmap the word proper, for maps between decent v-stacks that serve as 2-morphisms of correspondences or as proper pushforwards, means proper nice.
hypotheses: f : X → Y is a map of decent v-stacks.
Proper is in the sense of Sch17 Definition 18.1.
proofSteps: 0-truncation: Sch17 Definition 10.7(iii) and Remark 10.8 (separated maps are 0-truncated), and Definition 18.1 (proper maps are separated).

A proper map is compactifiable (it is its own canonical compactification, DiamondSixOperations S0/compactifiable-iff-separated-open); for a separated map representable in locally spatial diamonds, fineness is compactifiability of locally finite dim.trg (VS6/fine-permanence (iv)).
Composition and base change: properness, representability in locally spatial diamonds and finiteness of dim.trg are each stable (Sch17 Proposition 18.3 and §13, DiamondSixOperations S0).
Rf_! = Rf_* for proper f in the eligible class (DiamondSixOperations S1/lower-shriek-quasicompact).

Whether every proper fine map of decent v-stacks is representable in locally spatial diamonds is not settled by the sources: decent 0-truncated v-sheaves need not be diamonds (Spd Z_p), and Gulotta–Hansen–Weinstein Proposition 4.3(i) leaves the relevant representability claim as an exercise; the general case is recorded as a gap and is not needed by any target here.
acceptance: Closed immersions of decent v-stacks and proper nice diamonds X → Spd C are proper nice.
The structure map [S/G_S] → S of a classifying stack of a nontrivial locally pro-p group is fine but not proper: it is not 0-truncated.

nodes.title: Prespatial diamonds
nodes.statement: A qcqs diamond X is prespatial if it contains a spatial subdiamond X₀ ⊂ X with X₀(K, O_K) = X(K, O_K) for every perfectoid field K; a diamond X is locally prespatial if it contains a locally spatial subdiamond X₀ with X₀ → X quasicompact and the same equality of (K, O_K)-points. A map of v-stacks is representable in (locally) prespatial diamonds if it is 0-truncated and its base change to every (locally) prespatial diamond is (locally) prespatial. Prespatial diamonds are exactly the qcqs locally prespatial ones; open subdiamonds of locally prespatial diamonds are locally prespatial; (locally) spatial diamonds are (locally) prespatial; fibre products of (locally) prespatial diamonds are (locally) prespatial; and the canonical compactification of a separated map representable in prespatial diamonds is proper and representable in prespatial diamonds.
hypotheses: Everything lives over the category Perf of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with its v-topology.
proofSteps: Pairs: for a prespatial pair (X₀, X) and a locally prespatial pair (Y₀, Y) over a map X → Y, (X₀ ×_Y Y₀, X) is again a pair, since quasicompact injections into locally spatial diamonds have locally spatial source (GHW22 Lemma 3.2; DiamondsAndVStacks D5).
The sanity checks (i)–(vi) follow from the pair calculus (GHW22 Lemma 3.4).

Compactifications: the canonical compactification X̄^{/Y} → Y is proper (Sch17 Proposition 18.7(vii), recorded in DiamondSixOperations S0/compactifiable-iff-separated-open) and has the same (K, O_K)-points as X, hence as X₀ (GHW22 Proposition 3.6).
acceptance: Every spatial diamond is prespatial, with X₀ = X.
The canonical compactification of a separated spatial diamond over Spa(C, C⁺) is prespatial, although it is not known to be spatial.

nodes.title: Cohomological amplitude for prespatial maps
nodes.statement: If f : X → Y is proper and representable in prespatial diamonds, Rf_* has cohomological amplitude at most 3·dim.trg f. If f is separated, representable in prespatial diamonds with dim.trg f < ∞, then Rf_* has amplitude at most 3·dim.trg f, and if moreover f is compactifiable, so does Rf_! = Rf̄_* ∘ j_!. For a separated spatial diamond X with |X| of Krull dimension d, the maximal Hausdorff quotient |X|^h has cohomological dimension at most d; quasicompact injections have pushforward of amplitude zero.
hypotheses: Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
f is a map of small v-stacks as stated.
proofSteps: Reduce to Y = Spd(C, C⁺) and X separated prespatial proper over Y with a sheaf A in degree 0 vanishing on the generic fibre, as in the proof of Sch17 Theorem 22.5 (DiamondSixOperations S1/compactification-cd-bound).
Factor f through |X|^h × Y; the first map is proper and representable in spatial diamonds, with amplitude ≤ 2·dim.trg f (DiamondSixOperations S1/spatial-compactification-cd-bound).
Bound the cohomology of |X|^h by the Krull dimension of the spatial X₀ (GHW22 Lemma 3.8, via Scheiderer's theorem for spectral spaces whose generizations form chains), giving the remaining dim.trg f.
Separated case: factor through the canonical compactification and use that quasicompact injections have exact pushforward (GHW22 Corollary 3.9, Lemma 3.10).
acceptance: For a proper prespatial curve over Spd C the amplitude of Rf_* is at most 3.
A quasicompact open immersion has Rj_* of amplitude zero.

nodes.title: Exceptional pushforward for weakly compactifiable maps
nodes.statement: A map of small v-stacks is strongly compactifiable if it is compactifiable, representable in prespatial diamonds and locally of finite dim.trg, and weakly compactifiable if it is compactifiable, representable in locally prespatial diamonds and its source has an open cover by pieces strongly compactifiable over the target. Both classes are stable under composition and base change; a map is strongly compactifiable iff it is weakly compactifiable and quasicompact; a proper weakly compactifiable map is strongly compactifiable; a strongly compactifiable f factors as a quasicompact open immersion j followed by a proper strongly compactifiable f̄. For weakly compactifiable f between coproducts of qcqs v-sheaves, Rf_! = h_! ∘ Rp_* ∘ j_! (j an open immersion, p proper strongly compactifiable, h a local isomorphism) is defined and satisfies composition, base change, the projection formula and commutes with colimits; it agrees with Scholze's Rf_! when f is representable in locally spatial diamonds.
hypotheses: Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
Everything lives over the category Perf of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with its v-topology.
proofSteps: Permanence (i)–(iv): base change and composition of compactifiability (DiamondSixOperations S0) and of representability in prespatial diamonds (VS7/prespatial-diamond); the factorisation is through the canonical compactification. GHW22 Lemma 3.12 leaves (i)–(iv) to the reader; they are planned here.

Base change on unbounded complexes and commutation with colimits for Rf_* and Rf̄_*: repeat the arguments of Sch17 §§21–22 with the amplitude bound of VS7/prespatial-cohomological-amplitude (GHW22 Lemma 3.12(v)).

Composition, base change and projection formula of Rf_! = Rf̄_* ∘ j_!: as in DiamondSixOperations S1 for spatial-eligible maps (S1/lower-shriek-base-change-qc, S1/projection-formula-qc, S1/lower-shriek-composition-qc), with prespatial in place of spatial.
Only the case of maps between coproducts of qcqs v-sheaves is needed; GHW22 Scholium 3.13 claims the full extension of Sch17 §§22–24 without details, and that general claim is not a target here.
acceptance: For f representable in spatial diamonds the construction is DiamondSixOperations S1/lower-shriek-quasicompact.

nodes.title: Enhanced operations for coproducts of qcqs v-sheaves
nodes.statement: On the category Vsh_qcqs of small coproducts of qcqs v-sheaves, with the class W of weakly compactifiable maps, there is a Liu–Zheng enhanced operation map whose value on X is the symmetric monoidal ∞-category D_ét(X, Λ), whose ∗-direction is Scholze's pullback and whose !-direction on g ∈ W is the Rg_! of VS7/weakly-compactifiable-shriek. Proper weakly compactifiable maps and separated local isomorphisms are admissible classes whose restricted multisimplicial nerve is categorically equivalent to that of W. Every surjection in Vsh_qcqs is of universal ⊗-descent, and every surjection that is weakly compactifiable, representable in locally spatial diamonds and cohomologically smooth is of universal !-codescent.
hypotheses: Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
Everything lives over the category Perf of perfectoid spaces of characteristic p with its v-topology.
proofSteps: Categorical gluing: show that proper weakly compactifiable maps P and separated local isomorphisms I are admissible and that every strongly compactifiable map factors as p ∘ q with p ∈ P, q quasicompact in I; deduce the equivalences of restricted nerves as in Liu–Zheng's gluing of restricted nerves (GHW22 Proposition 3.15).
Start from the map encoding X ↦ D_ét(X, Λ) with symmetric monoidal ∗-pullbacks (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E3/coherent-diagrams-of-ringed-topoi and E5:abstract/symmetric-monoidal-infinity-category).

Pass to right adjoints in the proper direction (adjointability from proper base change and projection formula, VS7/weakly-compactifiable-shriek) and to left adjoints in the local-isomorphism direction, by Liu–Zheng's partial adjoint theorem; transport along the equivalence of nerves (GHW22 Theorem 3.14).

Descent: D_ét is a v-sheaf of closed symmetric monoidal stable ∞-categories; codescent for smooth surjections follows by twisting !-pullbacks into ∗-pullbacks with the invertible Rf_n^!Λ (GHW22 Proposition 3.16).
The Liu–Zheng machinery (enhanced operation maps, multisimplicial nerves, the partial adjoint theorem, gluing of restricted nerves) has no owner in the atlas; it is recorded as a gap.

nodes.title: Exceptional functors for fine maps of decent v-stacks
nodes.statement: For a fine map f : X → Y of decent v-stacks there is a functor Rf_! : D_ét(X, Λ) → D_ét(Y, Λ) with right adjoint Rf^!, such that (1) Rf_! agrees with Scholze's when f is separated and representable in locally spatial diamonds; (2) f ↦ Rf_! is a pseudo-functor from the 2-category of decent v-stacks and fine maps to triangulated categories, so 2-morphisms α : f ⇒ g of fine maps induce isomorphisms α_! : Rf_! ≅ Rg_! and α^! : Rf^! ≅ Rg^! compatible with composition; (3) the projection formula Rf_!(A ⊗ f^*B) ≅ Rf_!A ⊗ B holds; (4) proper base change g^* Rf_! ≅ Rf′_! g̃^* holds for every Cartesian square of decent v-stacks with f fine; the whole structure is encoded by an enhanced operation map on decent v-stacks whose ∗-part is D_ét(−, Λ) with its symmetric monoidal pullbacks.
hypotheses: Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
f is a fine map of decent v-stacks.
proofSteps: First iteration of DESCENT: from coproducts of separated spatial diamonds to quasiseparated locally separated locally spatial diamonds, with surjections as atlases, étale and smooth maps as the auxiliary classes and fine maps as the !-class; the fibre-product condition is GHW22 Lemma 4.10 (VS7/enhanced-operations-for-qcqs-v-sheaves gives Input I).

Second iteration: to all locally separated locally spatial diamonds (GHW22 Lemma 4.11). Third iteration: to decent v-stacks with fine maps, atlases being surjections and the auxiliary class the smooth maps (GHW22 §4.5).

Each iteration is the DESCENT extension theorem of Liu–Zheng (GHW22 Theorem 4.9), whose hypotheses P0–P5bis follow from proper and smooth base change and the codescent of Proposition 3.16; the theorem itself belongs to the unowned Liu–Zheng machinery (gap).

Identify the values with D_ét(X, Λ), compatibly with tensor products and pullbacks, using that every atlas is a v-cover (GHW22 Proposition 4.12); identify g_! with Scholze's Rg_! for representable g by hypercover and quasicompact-open exhaustion (GHW22 Proposition 4.13).

Pass to homotopy categories for (1)–(5) of GHW22 Theorem 1.4; Rf_! preserves colimits between presentable categories, so Rf^! exists (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E3/adjoint-functor-theorem-and-localisations).
acceptance: For f : [S/G_S] → S, Rf_! is group homology twisted by Haar measures (VS8/classifying-stack-structure-map).
For f representable in nice diamonds the functors are those of DiamondSixOperations S2–S3.

nodes.title: The six-functor identities for fine maps
nodes.statement: For a fine map f : Y → X of decent v-stacks and A, B ∈ D_ét: (P1) f^*A ⊗ f^*B ≅ f^*(A ⊗ B); (P2) Rf_* RHom(f^*A, B) ≅ RHom(A, Rf_*B); (P3) Rf_!(A ⊗ f^*B) ≅ Rf_!A ⊗ B; (P4) RHom(Rf_!A, B) ≅ Rf_* RHom(A, Rf^!B); (P5) Rf^! RHom(A, B) ≅ RHom(f^*A, Rf^!B). For a Cartesian square with f fine, (BC1) g^* Rf_! ≅ Rf′_! g̃^* and, when g is fine, (BC2) Rg^! Rf_* ≅ Rf′_* Rg̃^!. For fine X₁ → S, X₂ → S and correspondences, the Künneth formula (c₂ ×_S d₂)_!(B₁ ⊠_S B₂) ≅ c₂!B₁ ⊠_S d₂!B₂ holds, and the exterior product ⊠_S is compatible with !-pullback by a natural map c₂^!A′₁ ⊠_S d₂^!A′₂ → (c₂ ×_S d₂)^!(A′₁ ⊠_S A′₂).
hypotheses: Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
All maps are maps of decent v-stacks; the shriek operations are those of VS7/fine-shriek-functors.
proofSteps: (P1), (P2) hold for all maps of small v-stacks (Sch17 Theorem 1.8).
(P3) and (BC1) are parts (3) and (4) of VS7/fine-shriek-functors.
(P4) and (P5) follow from (P3) and the adjunctions by the Yoneda lemma; (BC2) is the right adjoint of (BC1) applied to g (EnhancedDerivedSheaves E3/mates-and-beck-chevalley).
Künneth: factor c₂ ×_S d₂ as (c₂ × id) ∘ (id × d₂), apply (BC1) and (P3) twice; the !-pullback comparison is adjoint to the Künneth isomorphism.
GHW22 Theorem 1.4 states only agreement, pseudo-functoriality, (P3), (BC1) and the right adjoint; the remaining identities attributed to it by HKW22 Theorem 4.1.8 are derived here (sourceIssues).

f is proper nice.

nodes.title: Intrinsic cohomological smoothness for fine maps
nodes.statement: For a fine map f : X → Y of decent v-stacks, the following are equivalent: (1) f is ℓ-cohomologically smooth (VS6/fine-cohomologically-smooth); (2) Rf^!F_ℓ is invertible, Rf^!F_ℓ ⊗ f^*(−) → Rf^!(−) is an isomorphism, and both statements hold after every decent base change; (3) Rf^!F_ℓ is invertible and its formation commutes with every decent base change. For smooth f and Λ with nΛ = 0, Rf^!Λ is invertible, Rf^!Λ ⊗ f^* ≅ Rf^!, smooth base change g̃^*Rf^! ≅ Rf′^! g^* and f′^*Rg_! ≅ Rg̃_! f^* hold, and the twisted pullback agrees with the parent's exceptional pullback for smooth stacky maps (VS0/shriek-pullback-for-smooth-stacky-maps).
hypotheses: Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
f is a fine map of decent v-stacks; ℓ ≠ p prime.
proofSteps: (1) ⇒ (2): with charts a, b and a smooth top map g, b^*Rf^!F_ℓ is a twist of Rg^!Ra^!F_ℓ by invertible objects, hence invertible; invertibility is v-local (DiamondSixOperations S4/invertible-object, S4/smooth-twisted-pullback).
(2) ⇒ (1): pull back a chart of Y; the top map g composed with a chart h of the source has R(g∘h)^! = R(g∘h)^!F_ℓ ⊗ (g∘h)^*, so g ∘ h is smooth (GHW22 Proposition 4.14).

(1) ⇔ (3): reduce to compactifiable maps of locally spatial diamonds and use Fargues–Scholze Proposition IV.2.33 (smooth iff F_ℓ is ULA with invertible dualizing object, iff the dualizing object is invertible and commutes with base change).
Smooth base change follows from (2) and (BC1); agreement with the parent's construction: both are the twisted pullback along smooth charts.

nodes.statement: For a fine map f : X → S of decent v-stacks, K_{X/S} := Rf^!Λ ∈ D_ét(X, Λ); H^0(X, A) denotes Hom(Λ_X, A). When S is connected and f is proper nice, integration ∫_X : H^0(X, K_{X/S}) → H^0(S, Λ) = Λ is pushforward along f.

nodes.title: Smooth and complete modules over locally constant functions
nodes.statement: Let C(T, Λ) be the ring of locally constant functions T → Λ and C_c(T, Λ) the ideal of those with compact support; for a compact open U ⊂ T, 1_U is its characteristic function and 1_U·M ≅ C(U, Λ)⊗M is a C(T, Λ)-module. A C(T, Λ)-module M is smooth if M ⊗_{C(T,Λ)} C_c(T, Λ) → M is an isomorphism, equivalently colim_U 1_U·M → M is an isomorphism over compact opens U ordered by inclusion (every m equals 1_U·m for some compact open U); M is complete if M → lim_U 1_U·M is an isomorphism, with transition maps multiplication by 1_V. The functors M^s := colim_U 1_U·M and M^c := lim_U 1_U·M are projectors onto smooth and complete modules and restrict to mutually inverse equivalences between them.
hypotheses: T is a locally profinite set (Hausdorff, locally compact, totally disconnected); Λ is a discrete commutative ring.
proofSteps: 1_U·M is both a submodule of colim_U 1_U·M and of lim_U 1_U·M, and equals 1_U applied to either (HKW22 Lemma B.2.2): the transition maps are inclusions, respectively projections, compatible with multiplication by idempotents.
Hence (M^s)^s = M^s and (M^c)^c = M^c, and (M^s)^c ≅ M^c, (M^c)^s ≅ M^s (HKW22 Lemma B.2.3).
acceptance: For T finite, C_c(T, Λ) = C(T, Λ) = Λ^T and every module is smooth and complete.
For T = N discrete and M = Λ^N, M^s = Λ^{(N)} ≠ M while M is complete.

nodes.title: Sheaves on a locally profinite set as smooth modules
nodes.statement: Let R be the sheaf of rings U ↦ C(U, Λ) on T. For an R-module sheaf F and compact open U, restriction F(T) → F(U) is surjective, restricts to an isomorphism 1_U·F(T) ≅ F(U), and F(T) = lim_U F(U). The functors M ↦ F_M (F_M(U) = 1_U·M) and F ↦ M^s_F = colim_U F(U) (respectively M^c_F = lim_U F(U)) are mutually inverse equivalences between smooth (respectively complete) C(T, Λ)-modules and R-module sheaves on T, compatible with the equivalence of VS8/smooth-and-complete-modules, and F_M(T) = M^c. In particular sheaves of Λ-modules on T are smooth C(T, Λ)-modules, the constant sheaf Λ corresponding to C_c(T, Λ).
hypotheses: T is a locally profinite set (Hausdorff, locally compact, totally disconnected); Λ is a discrete commutative ring.
proofSteps: Compact opens form a basis closed under finite unions and intersections, so sheaves on T are sheaves on that basis.
A compact open U is clopen, so T = U ⊔ (T ∖ U) and F(T) = F(U) × F(T ∖ U); 1_U acts as the projection, giving surjectivity and 1_U·F(T) ≅ F(U) (HKW22 Lemma B.2.4).
The sheaf condition along the cover by compact opens gives F(T) = lim_U F(U); combine with VS8/smooth-and-complete-modules to get the two equivalences (HKW22 Lemma B.2.5).

The constant sheaf Λ corresponds to the smooth module C_c(T, Λ), with global sections C(T, Λ) = C_c(T, Λ)^c.

nodes.title: Distributions on a locally profinite set
nodes.statement: The Λ-module of Λ-valued distributions on T is Dist(T, Λ) := Hom_Λ(C_c(T, Λ), Λ). It is a C(T, Λ)-module by (φ·μ)(h) = μ(φh); its smooth part is the module of distributions supported on compact sets; for a group G acting continuously on T, G acts by translation and Dist(T, Λ)^G is the module of invariant distributions.
hypotheses: T is a locally profinite set (Hausdorff, locally compact, totally disconnected); Λ is a discrete commutative ring.
proofSteps: Dist(T, Λ) is the algebraic Λ-dual of the smooth module C_c(T, Λ) (VS8/smooth-and-complete-modules).

C_c(T, Λ) is spanned by the 1_U·a for compact open U and a ∈ Λ (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.1/locally-constant-compact-support), so a distribution is a finitely additive Λ-valued function on compact opens.

nodes.title: Operations on a constant locally profinite diamond
nodes.statement: For S a geometric point, T locally profinite and f : T_S = T × S → S, the map f is representable in nice diamonds and D_ét(T_S, Λ) is equivalent to the derived category of smooth C(T, Λ)-modules, the constant sheaf Λ corresponding to C_c(T, Λ). Under this identification f^*M = C_c(T, Λ) ⊗_Λ M, Rf_*M is the derived functor of M ↦ M^c, Rf_!M is the underlying Λ-module of M, and Rf^!M = RHom_Λ(C_c(T, Λ), M)^s; in particular H^0(T_S, Rf^!Λ) ≅ Dist(T, Λ).
hypotheses: S = Spd C for an algebraically closed perfectoid field C, or S = Spd k for an algebraically closed discrete field k of characteristic p; D_ét(S, Λ) is identified with D(Λ).
T is a locally profinite set (Hausdorff, locally compact, totally disconnected); Λ is a discrete commutative ring.
Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: T_S → S is representable in nice diamonds: T_S is locally a proper diamond of dim.trg 0 over S (DiamondsAndVStacks D4/compact-hausdorff-diamonds, DiamondSixOperations S1/proper-dim-zero-classification).

T_S has locally cohomological dimension zero, so D_ét(T_S, Λ) = D(T_{S,ét}, Λ), and the étale site of T_S is the site of the topological space T (DiamondSixOperations S1/proper-dim-zero-topological-comparison); apply VS8/sheaves-on-locally-profinite-sets.
f^* is the constant sheaf functor; Rf_* is global sections, M ↦ M^c by HKW22 Lemma B.2.5; Rf_! is compactly supported sections, colim over compact opens of F(U) = M^s = M.

Rf^! is the right adjoint of Rf_!: Hom_Λ(N, M) = Hom_{C(T,Λ)}(N, Hom_Λ(C_c(T, Λ), M)) for smooth N, and maps from a smooth module land in the smooth part; at M = Λ, H^0 = Hom_Λ(C_c(T, Λ), Λ) = Dist(T, Λ) (VS8/locally-profinite-distributions).
acceptance: For T finite, all four operations are the identity on Λ^T-modules up to the obvious identifications.
For T = Z_p, Rf^!Λ is the sheaf of distributions of DiamondSixOperations S5/profinite-quotient-upper-shriek.

nodes.title: The module of Haar measures
nodes.statement: For a locally profinite group G and a commutative ring Λ, Haar(G, Λ) is the Λ-module of left-invariant Λ-valued Haar measures, i.e. Hom_G(C_c(G, Λ), Λ) for the left-translation action; G acts on it through right translation, by the modulus character. If G has a compact open subgroup of pro-order invertible in Λ (for instance G locally pro-p and p ∈ Λ^×), Haar(G, Λ) is free of rank one, generated by the measure normalised on such a subgroup; its dual is Haar(G, Λ)^∗.
hypotheses: G is a locally profinite group; Λ is a commutative ring.
proofSteps: A left-invariant distribution is determined by its values on translates of a compact open subgroup U₀; finite additivity and invariance give μ(gU) = [U₀ : U]^{-1} μ(U₀) for U ≤ U₀ when [U₀ : U] is invertible (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.1/a-valued-haar-measure, existence and uniqueness of the normalised measure).
Right translation by g multiplies a left Haar measure by the modulus δ(g) (SR.2/modulus-character).
acceptance: For G finite, Haar(G, Λ) ≅ Λ via counting measure, with trivial G-action.
For G = Z_p and Λ = F_p, Haar(Z_p, F_p) = 0, since μ(Z_p) = p·μ(pZ_p).

nodes.title: Classifying stacks of locally pro-p groups are decent
nodes.statement: For G as in HKW22 Example 4.2.2 and S a geometric point, the classifying v-stack [S/G_S] is decent with chart X/G_S → [S/G_S], the quotient q : S → [S/G_S] is representable in nice diamonds, and for every closed subgroup H ⊂ G the map [S/H_S] → [S/G_S] is representable in nice diamonds and [S/H_S] is decent.
hypotheses: S = Spd C for an algebraically closed perfectoid field C, or S = Spd k for an algebraically closed discrete field k of characteristic p; D_ét(S, Λ) is identified with D(Λ).

G is a locally pro-p group admitting a free action on a separated locally spatial diamond X with a strictly surjective cohomologically smooth map X → S (for instance G closed in GL_n(E) for E finite over Q_p or F_p((t)), with X = GL_{n,E}^♢ × S).
proofSteps: Diagonal: S ×_{[S/G_S]} S ≅ G_S, and more generally the diagonal of [S/G_S] has fibres G-torsors, which are locally separated locally spatial diamonds (VS6/classifying-stack-of-group-diamond).
Chart: X → X/G_S is a G_S-torsor, so X/G_S ×_{[S/G_S]} S ≅ X, which is strictly surjective and cohomologically smooth over S; hence X/G_S → [S/G_S] is a chart.
q is a G_S-torsor, representable in nice diamonds; for H closed, [S/H_S] → [S/G_S] has fibres (G/H)_S, constant locally profinite diamonds (VS8/constant-locally-profinite-diamond-operations).
acceptance: For G = GL_n(Z_p), [S/G_S] is decent.
For G = Q_p^× ⊂ GL₁(Q_p), [S/G_S] is decent.

nodes.title: The four operations of the point of a classifying stack
nodes.statement: For q : S → [S/G_S], q^* identifies D_ét([S/G_S], Λ) with the derived category of smooth G-representations on Λ-modules (the parent's VS4/classifying-stack-equivalence), the action of g ∈ G on q^*M coming from the 2-morphism α_g : q ⇒ q. Under it: q^*M is M with the action forgotten; Rq_*M = C(G, M)^{G-sm} (smooth induction from the trivial group); Rq_!M = C_c(G, Λ) ⊗ M (compact induction); Rq^!M = Hom_G(C_c(G, Λ), M); in particular Rq^!Λ = Haar(G, Λ).
hypotheses: S = Spd C for an algebraically closed perfectoid field C, or S = Spd k for an algebraically closed discrete field k of characteristic p; D_ét(S, Λ) is identified with D(Λ).

G is a locally pro-p group admitting a free action on a separated locally spatial diamond X with a strictly surjective cohomologically smooth map X → S (for instance G closed in GL_n(E) for E finite over Q_p or F_p((t)), with X = GL_{n,E}^♢ × S).
Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: q^* is the parent's equivalence (Fargues–Scholze Theorem V.1.1) with g acting via α_g (VS6/two-morphism-adjunction-compatibility).
Rq_* is the right adjoint of restriction to the trivial group, i.e. smooth induction (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.2/smooth-induction, SR.2/frobenius-reciprocity).

Rq_!: base change along q (BC1) identifies q^*Rq_!M with the compactly supported sections of the constant sheaf on G_S, i.e. C_c(G, M) (VS8/constant-locally-profinite-diamond-operations); this is compact induction from the trivial group (SR.2/compact-induction).
Rq^! is the right adjoint of compact induction: Hom_G(C_c(G, Λ), M); at M = Λ it is Haar(G, Λ) (VS8/haar-module).
acceptance: For G finite, Rq_* = Rq_! = Λ[G] ⊗ − and Rq^! = q^* up to Haar(G, Λ) ≅ Λ.
For G = Z_p and M = Λ, Rq_*Λ = C(Z_p, Λ) and Rq^!Λ = Haar(Z_p, Λ).

nodes.title: Restriction, induction and compact induction as operations
nodes.statement: For H ⊂ G closed and q : [S/H_S] → [S/G_S]: q^* is restriction from G to H, Rq_* is smooth induction Ind_H^G, Rq_! is compact induction c-Ind_H^G; Rq^! equals restriction when H is open, and Rq^!M = Hom_{H′}(C_c(H′, Λ), M)^{H-sm} when G = H × H′.
hypotheses: S = Spd C for an algebraically closed perfectoid field C, or S = Spd k for an algebraically closed discrete field k of characteristic p; D_ét(S, Λ) is identified with D(Λ).

G is a locally pro-p group admitting a free action on a separated locally spatial diamond X with a strictly surjective cohomologically smooth map X → S (for instance G closed in GL_n(E) for E finite over Q_p or F_p((t)), with X = GL_{n,E}^♢ × S).
Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
H ⊂ G is a closed subgroup.
proofSteps: Underlying modules: q_H^*q^* = q_G^* and α_h = id_q ∗ β_h, so q^* is restriction (VS6/two-morphism-adjunction-compatibility); Rq_* is its right adjoint, smooth induction.

Rq_!: base change along q_G gives the descent of M along G → G/H as compactly supported H-equivariant functions, i.e. c-Ind_H^G M, with the G-action identified through the compatibility of base change with α_g (VS8/constant-locally-profinite-diamond-operations, SR.2/compact-induction).
H open: q is étale, Rq^! = q^*. Direct factor: c-Ind_H^G M ≅ M ⊠ C_c(H′, Λ), whose right adjoint is the stated smooth part of Hom_{H′}(C_c(H′, Λ), −).
acceptance: For H = 1 the statements reduce to VS8/classifying-stack-operations.
For G = H × H′ with H′ finite, Rq^!M = M as an H-representation (Haar(H′) ≅ Λ).

nodes.title: The structure map of a classifying stack
nodes.statement: f : [S/G_S] → S is fine and ℓ-cohomologically smooth; under VS8/classifying-stack-operations, f^*M is M with trivial action, Rf_*M is derived G-invariants RΓ(G, M) (smooth group cohomology), Rf_!M = (M ⊗ Haar(G, Λ))_G is derived coinvariants (group homology twisted by Haar measures), Rf^!M = Haar(G, Λ)^∗ ⊗ M with trivial action twisted by the dual Haar character, and K_{[S/G_S]/S} = Haar(G, Λ)^∗.
hypotheses: S = Spd C for an algebraically closed perfectoid field C, or S = Spd k for an algebraically closed discrete field k of characteristic p; D_ét(S, Λ) is identified with D(Λ).

G is a locally pro-p group admitting a free action on a separated locally spatial diamond X with a strictly surjective cohomologically smooth map X → S (for instance G closed in GL_n(E) for E finite over Q_p or F_p((t)), with X = GL_{n,E}^♢ × S).
Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: Fine and smooth: the chart X/G_S → [S/G_S] composed with f is X/G_S → S. For a compact open pro-p subgroup K, X/K_S → S is cohomologically smooth (DiamondSixOperations S5/free-quotient-smooth, K having pro-order prime to ℓ), and X/K_S → X/G_S is étale and surjective (its base change to X is X × G/K → X), so X/G_S → S is smooth; the square with the chart witnesses smoothness of f (VS6/fine-cohomologically-smooth).
Rf_* is right adjoint to f^*, the trivial-representation functor: derived invariants (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.0:derived-extension/derived-invariants).
Smoothness gives Rf^!M ≅ f^*M ⊗ Rf^!Λ (VS7/fine-smoothness-and-dualizing-objects); since f ∘ q = id, M = Rq^!Rf^!M = Haar(G, Λ) ⊗ Rf^!M, so Rf^!M = Haar(G, Λ)^∗ ⊗ M.
Rf_! is the left adjoint of Rf^!, i.e. derived coinvariants of the Haar twist.
acceptance: For G finite of order invertible in Λ, Rf_* = Rf_! = (−)^G.
For G = Z_p and M = Λ, Rf_*Λ = Λ in degree 0 (p invertible) and K = Haar(Z_p, Λ)^∗ ≅ Λ.

nodes.title: Dualizable objects and categorical traces
nodes.statement: Let (C, ⊗, 1) be a symmetric monoidal 2-category (a symmetric monoidal bicategory). An object X is dualizable if there are an object X^∨ and 1-morphisms ev_X : X^∨ ⊗ X → 1 and coev_X : 1 → X ⊗ X^∨ whose two zig-zag composites are isomorphic to the identities of X and X^∨. ΩC := End(1) is a 1-category. For an endomorphism e of a dualizable X, the trace is tr(e) := ev_X ∘ σ ∘ (e ⊗ id_{X^∨}) ∘ coev_X ∈ ΩC (σ the symmetry); for u : X → Y, v : Y → X the pairing is ⟨u, v⟩ := tr(v ∘ u), and dim(X) := tr(id_X). In a symmetric monoidal 1-category this is the trace of an endomorphism of an object with an exact pairing, valued in End(1).
hypotheses: (C, ⊗, 1) is a symmetric monoidal bicategory; in the 1-categorical case, a symmetric monoidal category.
proofSteps: The dual is unique up to equivalence, X^∨ is dualizable with dual X, and X ⊗ Y is dualizable with dual X^∨ ⊗ Y^∨ (LZ22 Remark 1.2).

− ⊗ X^∨ is right and left adjoint to − ⊗ X, so Hom(X, Y) exists and is Y ⊗ X^∨ (LZ22 Remark 1.3); conversely X is dualizable iff Hom(X, 1) and Hom(X, X) exist and X ⊗ Hom(X, 1) → Hom(X, X) is split epi (LZ22 Lemma 1.4).
Duals of morphisms u^∨ and the squares (1.1) give ⟨u, v⟩ ≅ ⟨v, u⟩ when X, Y are both dualizable (LZ22 Construction 1.6).
In the 1-categorical case the data are Mathlib's ExactPairing X X^∨ and the trace is a morphism 𝟙 ⟶ 𝟙.
acceptance: In finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field, tr(e) is the linear-algebra trace and dim(V) is the dimension.
In D(Λ), the trace of an endomorphism of a perfect complex is its alternating trace (VS9/perfect-complexes-are-dualizable).

nodes.title: Functoriality of traces in symmetric monoidal 2-categories
nodes.statement: For a square e′ ∘ f ⇒ f ∘ e in C (e, e′ endomorphisms of dualizable X, X′, a 2-morphism filling the square) with f right adjointable, there is a morphism tr(e) → tr(e′) in ΩC built from the unit and counit of f ⊣ f^! and the duality data; more generally pairings ⟨u, v⟩ → ⟨u′, v′⟩ for squares (1.2), and, for squares equipped with a splitting, without adjointability. These morphisms are compatible with vertical composition, so tr is a functor from the (2,1)-category of endomorphisms of dualizable objects with right-adjointable morphisms to ΩC. A symmetric monoidal functor preserves duals, traces, pairings and these morphisms.
hypotheses: C is a symmetric monoidal bicategory; f is right adjointable (Mathlib's Bicategory.Adjunction) where stated.
proofSteps: Construct the morphism by pasting coev_X ⇒ (f ⊗ f^{!∨}) ∘ coev_{X′} (from the counit of f), the given 2-morphism, and ev_{X′} ∘ (f ⊗ f^{!∨}) ⇒ ev_X (from the unit) (LZ22 Construction 1.7, equations (1.3)–(1.4)).
Without adjointability, decompose a split square and use the case f = id twice (LZ22 Construction 1.8).
Functoriality in vertical composition is the coherence of mates (Mathlib's bicategorical mates; LZ22 cites Hoyois–Scherotzke–Sibilla §2.1).
Symmetric monoidal functors preserve all the data since they preserve the duality equations (LZ22 Remark 1.9).
acceptance: For a 1-category C every square with invertible 2-cell gives an equality tr(e) = tr(e′) when f is an isomorphism.
Applied to a symmetric monoidal base change functor it gives the base change of local terms (VS10/local-terms-base-change).

nodes.title: The symmetric monoidal Grothendieck construction
nodes.statement: For a symmetric monoidal 2-category B and a right-lax symmetric monoidal functor F : B → Cat^co (Cat with 2-morphisms reversed), with unit e_F ∈ F(1) and exterior products ⊠ : F(X) × F(X′) → F(X ⊗ X′), the Grothendieck construction C_F has objects (X, L) with L ∈ F(X), morphisms (c, u) with c : X → Y and u : F(c)L → M, 2-morphisms p : c ⇒ d compatible with u, v through F(p), and tensor (X, L) ⊗ (X′, L′) = (X ⊗ X′, L ⊠ L′). For a 2-morphism p from c to a square g ∘ c ⇒ c′ ∘ f and (c, u) above c, there is a unique (c′, u′) above c′ such that p is a 2-morphism (X, L) → (Y′, F(g)M) in C_F. If f : X → X′ is right adjointable in B, so is f♮ = (f, id) : (X, L) → (X′, F(f)L); if moreover the F_{c,c′} are isomorphisms, (X, L) is dualizable in C_F and X′ is dualizable in B, then (X′, F(f)L) is dualizable with dual (X′^∨, F(f^{!∨})L^∨). Right-lax symmetric monoidal transformations and functors induce right-lax symmetric monoidal functors of Grothendieck constructions.
hypotheses: B is a symmetric monoidal bicategory; F is right-lax symmetric monoidal.
proofSteps: Objects, morphisms, 2-morphisms and tensor products are as in LZ22 Construction 1.10.
Uniqueness of the pushed morphism: u′ is forced to be F(c′)F(f)L ≅ F(c′f)L → F(gc)L ≅ F(g)F(c)L → F(g)M (LZ22 Lemma 1.11).
Adjointability and dualizability transfer: write the unit and counit of f♮ from those of f and the duality data of (X, L) through F (LZ22 Remark 1.12).

nodes.title: Dualizable objects of D(Λ) and their traces
nodes.statement: For any commutative ring Λ and M ∈ D(Λ) with 𝔻M := RHom(M, Λ[0]), the following are equivalent: (a) M → 𝔻𝔻M and 𝔻M ⊗ M → 𝔻(M ⊗ 𝔻M) are isomorphisms; (b) M ⊗ 𝔻M → RHom(M, M) is an isomorphism; (c) M is strongly dualizable, i.e. N ⊗ 𝔻M → RHom(M, N) is an isomorphism for all N; (d) M is compact; (e) M is perfect. Then 𝔻M is a dual of M, and the categorical trace of an endomorphism f of M is its Euler-characteristic trace Σ_i (−1)^i tr(f^i | P^i) for any bounded complex P of finitely generated projective modules representing M with a chain endomorphism lifting f.
hypotheses: Λ is a commutative ring; ⊗ is the derived tensor product.
proofSteps: (a) ⇒ (b): RHom(M, M) ≅ RHom(M, 𝔻𝔻M) ≅ 𝔻(M ⊗ 𝔻M) ≅ 𝔻M ⊗ M.
(b) ⇒ (c): the identity gives a coevaluation Λ → M ⊗ 𝔻M, from which the inverse of N ⊗ 𝔻M → RHom(M, N) is built (HKW22 Lemma B.1.2(2)).
(c) ⇔ (d) ⇔ (e): EnhancedDerivedSheaves E5:spectra-comparison/perfect-modules (perfect = compact = dualizable).
(e) ⇒ (a): compute on a bounded complex of finitely generated projectives, localising to free modules of finite rank.

Trace: with P as stated, the categorical trace of the chain map is computed degreewise with the Koszul sign of the symmetry, giving the alternating sum of the traces of the f^i (LinearMap.trace on each P^i after localisation to free modules).
acceptance: For M = Λ^n[0] and f a matrix, tr(f) is the matrix trace.
For M = Λ ⊕ Λ[1] and f = id, tr(f) = 0 = χ(M).

sources.match: States that dualizable objects of D(Λ) are the perfect complexes with dual RHom(M, Λ[0]) and trace the Euler characteristic, and proves the equivalence of (a)–(e).

nodes.title: Reflexivity over truncated discrete valuation rings
nodes.statement: Let R be a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal 𝔪 and Λ = R/𝔪^k (k ≥ 1). For a Λ-module M the canonical map M → M^∗∗ (M^∗ = Hom_Λ(M, Λ)) is an isomorphism iff M is finitely generated. Consequently, for M ∈ D(Λ) the map M → 𝔻𝔻M is an isomorphism iff every H^i(M) is finitely generated.
hypotheses: R is a discrete valuation ring; k ≥ 1; Λ = R/𝔪^k.
proofSteps: If M is finitely generated it is a finite sum of cyclic Λ-modules, each reflexive.

Converse by induction on k: Λ is self-injective (Artinian serial), so dualizing is exact; compare the sequences 0 → 𝔪M → M → M/𝔪M → 0 and their double duals; M/𝔪M is reflexive over κ = R/𝔪, hence finite-dimensional; the snake lemma makes 𝔪M reflexive over R/𝔪^{k−1} (HKW22 Lemma B.1.1, with the index corrected in sourceIssues).
Derived version: self-injectivity gives H^i(𝔻M) ≅ H^{−i}(M)^∗, so H^i(𝔻𝔻M) ≅ H^i(M)^∗∗ (HKW22 Lemma B.1.2(1)).
acceptance: For Λ = Z/ℓ² and M = Z/ℓ ⊕ Z/ℓ², M ≅ M^∗∗.
For Λ = Z/ℓ and M = Λ^(ℕ), M → M^∗∗ is injective but not surjective.
The module-level statement is the suggested declaration `bijective_dual_eval_iff_finite`, with Module.Dual.eval over R ⧸ 𝔪^k.

sources.locator: Lemma B.1.1 and Lemma B.1.2(1), pp. 72–73
sources.match: Proves that over R/𝔪^k a module is reflexive iff finitely generated, and the derived consequence for the biduality map.

nodes.title: The symmetric monoidal 2-category of correspondences
nodes.statement: For a decent v-stack S, Corr_S has objects the decent S-v-stacks X with fine structure map; 1-morphisms X → X′ are correspondences X ← C → X′ (c₁, c₂) of decent v-stacks over S with c₂ fine (then c₁ and C → S are fine), composed by fibre product C ×_{X′} D; 2-morphisms c ⇒ d are equivalence classes of triples (p, α₁, α₂) with p : C → D proper nice (VS6/proper-nice-maps) and 2-isomorphisms α_i : c_i ⇒ d_i ∘ p, two triples being equivalent when a 2-isomorphism γ : p ⇒ q satisfies β_i = (id_{d_i} ∗ γ) ∘ α_i. The tensor product is X ⊗ Y = X ×_S Y with unit S, and c ⊗ d = c ×_S d. ΩCorr_S is the 1-category of decent v-stacks fine over S with proper nice maps over S.
hypotheses: S is a decent v-stack.
Proper 2-morphisms are proper nice maps (VS6/proper-nice-maps): proper in the sense of Sch17 Definition 18.1, hence 0-truncated, and representable in locally spatial diamonds.
proofSteps: Compositions and tensor products stay in Corr_S by VS6/decent-fibre-products and VS6/fine-permanence; associativity and unit constraints come from the universal property of fibre products of stacks.
Well-definedness of the equivalence relation on 2-morphisms and their compositions uses the strict (2,1)-category structure of v-stacks (HKW22 §4.1, p. 22).

For a proper nice q : X → X′ over S, the 1-morphism q♮ = (id, q) : X → X′ is right adjointable, with right adjoint (q, id), unit given by the diagonal X → X ×_{X′} X (proper since q is separated) and counit by q itself (the analogue of LZ22 Lemma 2.9).
acceptance: End(1) = ΩCorr_S: correspondences S ← C → S are decent v-stacks C fine over S, and 2-morphisms are proper maps over S.
For q proper nice, the unit of q♮ ⊣ q♮^! is the diagonal of X over X′.

nodes.title: The symmetric monoidal 2-category of cohomological correspondences
nodes.statement: CoCorr_S has objects (X, A) with X ∈ Corr_S and A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ); 1-morphisms (X, A) → (X′, A′) are pairs (c, u) with c a correspondence and u : c₁^*A → c₂^!A′, composed as (d′₁)^*c₁^*A → (d′₁)^*c₂^!A′ → (c′₂)^!d₁^*A′ → (c′₂)^!d₂^!A″ (the middle map adjoint to base change); 2-morphisms (c, u) ⇒ (d, v) are the 2-morphisms (p, α₁, α₂) of Corr_S for which the composite d₁^*A → p_*p^*d₁^*A ≅ p_*c₁^*A → p_*c₂^!A′ ≅ p_*p^!d₂^!A′ ≅ p_!p^!d₂^!A′ → d₂^!A′ equals v. The tensor product is (X, A) ⊗ (X′, A′) = (X ×_S X′, A ⊠_S A′) with unit (S, Λ_S), and (c, u) ⊗ (d, v) uses the Künneth map into (c₂ ×_S d₂)^!(A′₁ ⊠_S A′₂). The monoidal structure is closed with Hom((X₁, A₁), (X₂, A₂)) = (X₁ ×_S X₂, RHom(pr₁^*A₁, pr₂^!A₂)). Equivalently, CoCorr_S is the Grothendieck construction of the right-lax symmetric monoidal functor Corr_S → Cat^co, X ↦ D_ét(X, Λ), c ↦ c₂!c₁^*. ΩCoCorr_S has objects (X, ω) with X fine over S and ω ∈ H^0(X, K_{X/S}), and morphisms proper p with p_∗ω = ω′.
hypotheses: S is a decent v-stack; Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
The exceptional functors are those of VS7/fine-shriek-functors; proper 2-morphisms use Rp_∗ = Rp_! (VS7/proper-nice-shriek-is-pushforward).
proofSteps: Composition and its associativity: base change (BC1) and its compatibility with composition (VS7/fine-six-functor-identities).

2-morphisms depend only on the equivalence class of (p, α₁, α₂): the five squares of HKW22 p. 30 commute by VS6/two-morphism-adjunction-compatibility, by β_i = (id ∗ γ) ∘ α_i with the pseudo-functor structures, and by γ_∗ = γ_! for proper maps.
Tensor products: the Künneth isomorphism (c₂ ×_S d₂)_!(B₁ ⊠_S B₂) ≅ c₂!B₁ ⊠_S d₂!B₂ (VS7/fine-six-functor-identities); the target is (c₂ ×_S d₂)^!(A′₁ ⊠_S A′₂) (HKW22 misprint E14 corrected).
Closedness: Hom from (X, A) ⊗ (Y, B) to (Z, C) and from (X, A) to (Y ×_S Z, RHom(pr^*B, pr^!C)) agree through RHom(a ⊗ b, c) ≅ RHom(a, RHom(b, c)) and (P5) (the analogue of LZ22 Lemma 2.8).

Grothendieck construction: the functor X ↦ D_ét(X, Λ), c ↦ c₂!c₁^*, p ↦ counit, is right-lax symmetric monoidal with Künneth isomorphisms; apply VS9/symmetric-monoidal-grothendieck-construction (LZ22 Remark 2.7).

nodes.title: Dualizability in cohomological correspondences
nodes.statement: For X fine over S and A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ), (X, A) is dualizable in CoCorr_S iff the natural map m : 𝔻_{X/S}A ⊠_S A → RHom(pr₁^*A, pr₂^!A) on X ×_S X is an isomorphism, where 𝔻_{X/S}A = RHom(A, K_{X/S}). Then the dual is (X, 𝔻_{X/S}A), evaluation lies over (Δ_{X/S}, π) with Δ^*(𝔻A ⊠ A) ≅ 𝔻A ⊗ A → K_{X/S}, and coevaluation lies over (π, Δ_{X/S}) with Λ_X → RHom(A, A) ≅ Δ^!RHom(pr₁^*A, pr₂^!A) followed by m^{-1}.
hypotheses: S is a decent v-stack; Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
π : X → S is fine.
proofSteps: The candidate evaluation 𝔢 induces 𝔛′ ⊗ 𝔜 → Hom(𝔛, 𝔜) for every 𝔜; for 𝔜 = 𝔛 it is m (VS9/cohomological-correspondence-bicategory, internal Hom).
If 𝔛 is dualizable, 𝔛^∨ ⊗ 𝔜 → Hom(𝔛, 𝔜) is an isomorphism for all 𝔜 (VS9/dualizable-object-and-trace); 𝔜 = 1 identifies 𝔛^∨ with (X, 𝔻A) and 𝔜 = 𝔛 makes m an isomorphism.
Conversely define the coevaluation through (P5) and m^{-1} and check the triangle identities by a diagram chase (HKW22 Proposition 4.3.5).

(X, Λ_X) for X smooth fine over S is dualizable with dual (X, K_{X/S}).

nodes.title: Dualizable objects are the universally locally acyclic ones

For π representable in nice diamonds this is Fargues–Scholze Theorem IV.2.23; in general ULA-ness and the criterion of VS9/dualizability-criterion are both cohomologically-smooth-local on the source. Duals of ULA objects are ULA and the biduality map is an isomorphism; exterior products over S of ULA objects are ULA.
hypotheses: S is a decent v-stack; Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
π : X → S is fine.
proofSteps: Representable case: the criterion of VS9/dualizability-criterion is condition (ii) of Fargues–Scholze Theorem IV.2.23, equivalent to ULA (the parent's VS1/ula-dualizability-criterion).

nodes.title: The relative Lefschetz–Verdier trace formula for v-stacks
nodes.statement: Let 𝔛 = (X, A) be dualizable in CoCorr_S and 𝔣 ∈ End(𝔛) lie over c : C → X ×_S X. Suppose given proper nice maps q : X → X′ and p : C → C′ over S and a correspondence C′ → X′ ×_S X′ such that the square formed by c, c′, p and q × q commutes. Then 𝔛′ = (X′, Rq_∗A) is dualizable; there is a unique 𝔣′ ∈ End(𝔛′) lying over C′ such that p defines a 2-morphism p̃ filling the square 𝔣′ ∘ 𝔮 ⇒ 𝔮 ∘ 𝔣 (𝔮 the 1-morphism over q); and there is a unique 2-morphism tr(p̃) : tr(𝔣) ⇒ tr(𝔣′) lying over tr(p) : Fix(c) → Fix(c′). Concretely, the induced proper map Fix(c) → Fix(c′) pushes tr_c(u, A) to tr_{c′}(u′, Rq_∗A).
hypotheses: S is a decent v-stack; Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
q : X → X′ and p : C → C′ are proper nice maps over S (VS6/proper-nice-maps) compatible with the correspondences.
proofSteps: Uniqueness and existence of 𝔣′: lift (c, u) along the 2-morphism given by p (VS9/symmetric-monoidal-grothendieck-construction, Lu–Zheng Lemma 1.11; VS9/cohomological-correspondence-bicategory, pushAlongProper).

Dualizability of (X′, Rq_∗A): q♮ is right adjointable in Corr_S (VS9/correspondence-bicategory) and X′ is dualizable in Corr_S, so Lu–Zheng Remark 1.12(b) applies; equivalently (X′, Rq_∗A) has dual (X′, Rq_∗𝔻_{X/S}A) by the internal-Hom argument of Lu–Zheng Proposition 2.23.

The two triangles coev_{𝔛′} ⇒ (𝔮 ⊗ 𝔮^∨) ∘ coev_𝔛 and ev_𝔛 ⇒ ev_{𝔛′} ∘ (𝔮 ⊗ 𝔮^∨) and the square p̃ ⊗ id_{𝔮^∨} paste to tr(p̃) (VS9/trace-functoriality, Lu–Zheng Construction 1.7); uniqueness holds because 2-morphisms in CoCorr_S over a given proper map are unique.
The concrete form reads off the 2-morphism in ΩCoCorr_S (VS9/cohomological-correspondence-bicategory, omega).

Fix(c)_T = Fix(c_T), and the induced map H^0(Fix(c), K_{Fix(c)/S}) → H^0(Fix(c)_T, K_{Fix(c)_T/T}) is compatible with H^0(S, Λ) → H^0(T, Λ).

nodes.statement: For M ∈ D_ét([S/G_S], Λ) the following are equivalent: (1) ([S/G_S], M) is dualizable in CoCorr_S, with dual ([S/G_S], 𝔻M), 𝔻M = Haar(G, Λ)^∗ ⊗ M^∨, where M^∨ = RHom(M, Λ) is the derived smooth dual; (2) M is ULA over S; (3) for every compact open pro-p subgroup K ⊂ G the derived invariants M^K form a perfect complex of Λ-modules. The Verdier dual is RHom(M, f^!Λ) with f^!Λ = Haar(G, Λ)^∗ (VS8/classifying-stack-structure-map), and RHom(M, Λ) is the derived smooth dual (Fargues–Scholze Corollary V.1.4; SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.0:derived-extension/derived-smooth-dual).

(2) ⇔ (3): adapt Fargues–Scholze's proof of Theorem V.7.1 from Bun_G to [S/G_S], as HKW22 indicate: by Fargues–Scholze Proposition IV.2.32, ULA-ness is the isomorphism p₁^*RHom(M, Λ) ⊗ p₂^*M ≅ RHom(p₁^*M, p₂^*M) on [S/G_S] ×_S [S/G_S] = [S/(G × G)_S]. Test it against the compact generators c-Ind_{K×K}^{G×G}Λ, K pro-p open (SR.0:derived-extension/compact-generation): the left side gives (M^∨)^K ⊗ M^K = RHom(M^K, Λ) ⊗ M^K (invariants of pro-p groups are exact, and 𝔻(V)^K ≅ RHom(V^K, Λ) by SR.0:derived-extension/derived-smooth-dual), the right side gives Hom(M_K, M^K) = RHom(M^K, M^K) (coinvariants equal invariants for pro-p K), so the comparison at level K is the map of VS9/perfect-complexes-are-dualizable (b), an isomorphism iff M^K is perfect. The parent proves the Bun_G case (VS5/ula-equals-admissibility).

Direct proof of (3) ⇒ (1): the coevaluation over (f, Δ_f) is the G × G-equivariant integration map I : C_c(G, Λ) ⊗ Haar(G, Λ) → H^0(M ⊗ M^∨), I(h ⊗ μ) = ∫ h(g) g dμ(g), which factors through End(M^K) for K small; the explicit description of Δ_f^! uses VS8/restriction-and-induction-as-operations (G is a direct factor of G × G via the diagonal).
acceptance: A smooth representation M placed in degree 0 whose invariants M^K are finite projective Λ-modules for all open pro-p K is admissible.
The regular representation C_c(G, Λ) of a noncompact G is not admissible: its K-invariants are not finitely generated.

nodes.title: The inertia stack of a classifying stack
nodes.statement: In_S([S/G_S]) ≅ [G_S//G_S], the quotient of G_S by conjugation: a Y-point is a G_S-torsor Ỹ → Y with a G-equivariant automorphism y ↦ φ(y)·y, φ(gy) = gφ(y)g^{-1}. Combined with VS8/quotients-of-locally-profinite-sets for the conjugation action this gives H^0(In_S([S/G_S]), K_{In_S([S/G_S])/S}) ≅ Hom_G(C_c(G, Λ) ⊗ Haar(G, Λ), Λ), with G acting on C_c(G, Λ) by conjugation and on Haar(G, Λ) by the modulus character.
hypotheses: S is a geometric point (Spd C or Spd k); Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
G is a locally pro-p group as in HKW22 Example 4.2.2 (e.g. closed in GL_n(E)); D_ét([S/G_S], Λ) is the derived category of smooth G-representations.
proofSteps: Unwind In_S(X) = X ×_{X ×_S X} X for X = [S/G_S] through VS6/classifying-stack-of-group-diamond: an automorphism of a torsor commuting with the action is given by a conjugation-equivariant map to G.
[G_S//G_S] = [T_S/G_S] for T = G with the conjugation action; apply VS8/quotients-of-locally-profinite-sets.
acceptance: For G finite, In_S([S/G]) = ⊔ over conjugacy classes of [S/Z_G(g)].
For G abelian, In_S([S/G_S]) = G_S × [S/G_S].

nodes.title: Trace distributions of admissible objects
nodes.statement: For M admissible on [S/G_S], h ∈ C_c(G, Λ) and μ ∈ Haar(G, Λ), the operator I_{h,μ}(v) = ∫_G h(g) g v dμ(g) on M factors through the perfect complex M^K for K pro-p open with h bi-K-invariant; the trace distribution tr.dist(M) ∈ Hom_G(C_c(G, Λ) ⊗ Haar(G, Λ), Λ) sends h ⊗ μ to the Euler-characteristic trace of I_{h,μ} on M^K, independent of K. G acts on C_c(G, Λ) by conjugation and on Haar(G, Λ) by the modulus character, and tr.dist(M) is invariant.
hypotheses: S is a geometric point (Spd C or Spd k); Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
G is a locally pro-p group as in HKW22 Example 4.2.2 (e.g. closed in GL_n(E)); D_ét([S/G_S], Λ) is the derived category of smooth G-representations.
M is admissible (VS11/admissible-objects-on-classifying-stacks).
proofSteps: For K pro-p, M^K is a direct summand of M via averaging with a normalised Haar measure (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.0:abelian-category/averaging-projector).
Integration against h dμ is the action of the Hecke algebra (SR.1/integration, SR.1/convolution-algebra); for bi-K-invariant h it preserves M^K and is zero on its complement.
Independence of K: for K′ ⊂ K, the trace on M^{K′} equals that on M^K since I_{h,μ} has image in M^K (cyclicity of traces, VS9/dualizable-object-and-trace).
Invariance: conjugating h by g and translating μ intertwines I_{h,μ} with g I g^{-1}.
acceptance: For G finite and μ counting measure, tr.dist(M)(h ⊗ μ) = Σ_g h(g) tr(g | M).
For M = M₁ ⊕ M₂, tr.dist is additive.

sources.locator: §4.4, equation (4.4.1), p. 35; proof of Proposition 4.4.1, pp. 34–35
sources.match: Defines the trace distribution of an admissible object as h ⊗ μ ↦ Euler characteristic of I_{h,μ}, which factors through the perfect complex M^K.

nodes.title: The characteristic class of an admissible object is its trace distribution
nodes.statement: For M admissible on [S/G_S], under the identification of VS11/inertia-of-classifying-stack, cc_{[S/G_S]/S}(M) = tr.dist(M).
hypotheses: S is a geometric point (Spd C or Spd k); Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
G is a locally pro-p group as in HKW22 Example 4.2.2 (e.g. closed in GL_n(E)); D_ét([S/G_S], Λ) is the derived category of smooth G-representations.
M is admissible.
proofSteps: cc(M) = ev ∘ coev applied to id_M (VS9/inertia-and-characteristic-class).

Under H^0(RHom(M, M)) ≅ End_G(M), H^0(Δ_f^!(𝔻M ⊠ M)) ≅ Hom_{G×G}(C_c(G, Λ) ⊗ Haar(G, Λ), M^∨ ⊠ M) and H^0(K_{In}) ≅ Hom_G(C_c(G, Λ) ⊗ Haar(G, Λ), Λ), coevaluation sends id to the integration map I and evaluation sends I to h ⊗ μ ↦ tr(I_{h,μ}) (HKW22 proof of Proposition 4.4.3, using the explicit coevaluation of VS11/admissible-objects-on-classifying-stacks).
acceptance: For G finite, cc(M) is the character of M.
For M = Λ and G compact pro-p, cc(Λ) is the Haar distribution.

nodes.title: The modified Künneth map
nodes.statement: Let U → T be a cohomologically smooth map of decent S-v-stacks and f_i : Y_i → X_i (i = 1, 2) fine maps fitting in 2-commutative squares over U → T, with f : Y₁ ×_U Y₂ → X₁ ×_T X₂ and g : Y₁ ×_U Y₂ → U. For A_i ∈ D_ét(X_i, Λ), κ_{U/T} : f₁^!A₁ ⊠_U f₂^!A₂ → f^!(A₁ ⊠_T A₂) ⊗ g^*K_{U/T} is the composite of (Δ′_{U/T})^*(f₁^!A₁ ⊠_T f₂^!A₂), the Künneth map into (Δ′)^*(f₁ ×_T f₂)^!(A₁ ⊠_T A₂), the identification g^*(Δ_{U/T})^!Λ ⊗ g^*K_{U/T} ≅ Λ of Lemma 4.1.11, the map (Δ′)^* ⊗ (Δ′)^!Λ → (Δ′)^! of (4.1.2), and (Δ′)^!(f₁ ×_T f₂)^! = f^!. For X₁ = X₂ = T = S it is κ_{U/S} : K_{Y₁/S} ⊠_U K_{Y₂/S} → K_{Y₁×_UY₂/S} ⊗ g^*K_{U/S}.
hypotheses: S is a decent v-stack; Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
U → T is cohomologically smooth; f₁, f₂ are fine.
proofSteps: The Cartesian square Y₁ ×_U Y₂ → Y₁ ×_T Y₂ over Δ_{U/T} : U → U ×_T U identifies ⊠_U with (Δ′)^* of ⊠_T.
Each displayed map is an instance of VS7/fine-six-functor-identities (Künneth), VS7/diagonal-dualizing-complex and the natural transformation (4.1.2) (VS7/fine-smoothness-and-dualizing-objects).
acceptance: For U = T, κ_{T/T} is the Künneth map f₁^!A₁ ⊠_T f₂^!A₂ → (f₁ ×_T f₂)^!(A₁ ⊠_T A₂).
For Y_i = X_i, f_i = id and U = T, κ is the identity.

nodes.title: Canonical trivialisation over the inertia of a smooth base
nodes.statement: If T is a decent S-v-stack whose structure map π : T → S and diagonal Δ_{T/S} are both cohomologically smooth (e.g. T = [S/G] for a cohomologically smooth locally spatial group diamond G), then (T, Λ_T) is dualizable in CoCorr_S, In_S(T) → S is cohomologically smooth, and cc_{T/S}(Λ_T), viewed as a map Λ_{In_S(T)} → K_{In_S(T)/S}, is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: S is a decent v-stack; Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
π and Δ_{T/S} are cohomologically smooth.
proofSteps: In_S(T) is a base change of Δ_{T/S}, so smooth over T and hence over S.

The coevaluation map π^*Λ ≅ Δ^!pr₁^!π^*Λ ≅ Δ^!pr₂^*π^!Λ is an isomorphism by smoothness of π (VS7/fine-smoothness-and-dualizing-objects); the evaluation Δ^*pr₂^*K_{T/S} → π^!Λ is an isomorphism with no hypotheses.
cc_{T/S}(Λ_T) = h^*Δ^!pr₂^*K ≅ h^!Δ^*pr₂^*K ≅ h^!K_{T/S} ≅ K_{In_S(T)/S}, the middle isomorphism by smooth base change for the smooth Δ (HKW22 Lemma 4.5.2).
acceptance: For T = [S/G] with G finite étale, In_S(T) is a finite union of classifying stacks and K is trivial.
For T = S, the statement is cc_{S/S}(Λ) = 1.

sources.locator: Lemma 4.5.2 and proof, pp. 37–38, with the preceding diagram
sources.match: Proves dualizability of (T, Λ_T) and that its characteristic class canonically trivialises K_{In_S(T)/S} when π and Δ_{T/S} are smooth.

nodes.title: Based cohomological correspondences
nodes.statement: BCoCorr_S has objects (X → T, A, B) with X → T a fine map of decent S-v-stacks fine over S, T → S cohomologically smooth, A ∈ D_ét(X, Λ) and B ∈ D_ét(T, Λ) invertible; morphisms (q♮, α, β) with q♮ = (p, q, p′) a morphism of correspondences C → X ×_U X′ over U → T ×_S T′ (u′ : U → T′ cohomologically smooth), α : c^*A → c′^!A′ and β : u^*B ≅ u′^!B′ an isomorphism; 2-morphisms pairs of proper maps C → D and U → V compatible as in Definition 4.3.4; tensor (X → T, A, B) ⊗ (X′ → T′, A′, B′) = (X ×_S X′ → T ×_S T′, A ⊠_S A′, B ⊠_S B′). Base and source functors 𝔅(X → T, A, B) = (T, B) and 𝔖(X → T, A, B) = (X, A) are symmetric monoidal to CoCorr_S. For objects with a common base 𝔗 = (T, B), 𝔛₁ ⊠_𝔗 𝔛₂ := (X₁ ×_T X₂ → T, (A₁ ⊠_T A₂) ⊗ p^*B^{-1}, B); on morphisms lying over a common morphism of bases it uses (α₁ ⊠_U α₂) ⊗ β, the modified Künneth map κ_{U/T′} and Lemma 4.1.10 (equation (4.5.7)).
hypotheses: S is a decent v-stack; Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: Composition of morphisms as in VS9/cohomological-correspondence-bicategory, with smoothness of u′ preserved under composition (VS6/fine-cohomologically-smooth).
The fibre product on morphisms is the composite (4.5.7) built from VS11/modified-kunneth-map and VS7/shriek-and-invertible-objects.
Its functoriality and monoidality (4.5.8)–(4.5.9) are VS11/based-fibre-product-coherence.
acceptance: For T = S and B = Λ, BCoCorr_S restricts to CoCorr_S via 𝔖.
𝔅 and 𝔖 send the unit (S → S, Λ, Λ) to (S, Λ).

nodes.title: Functoriality and monoidality of fibre products over a base
nodes.statement: The fibre product ⊠_𝔗 is a functor BCoCorr_S ×_{𝔅, CoCorr_S} BCoCorr_S → BCoCorr_S: there are coherent 2-isomorphisms (𝔣′₁ ⊠_{e′} 𝔣′₂) ∘ (𝔣₁ ⊠_e 𝔣₂) ≅ (𝔣′₁ ∘ 𝔣₁) ⊠_{e′∘e} (𝔣′₂ ∘ 𝔣₂), and it is monoidal: (𝔛₁ ⊠_𝔗 𝔛₂) ⊗ (𝔛′₁ ⊠_{𝔗′} 𝔛′₂) ≅ (𝔛₁ ⊗ 𝔛′₁) ⊠_{𝔗⊗𝔗′} (𝔛₂ ⊗ 𝔛′₂), compatibly with the symmetry and the 𝔅- and 𝔖-images.
hypotheses: S is a decent v-stack; Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
proofSteps: Composition: the composite of two diagrams (4.5.6) is the diagram for the composite; the 2-isomorphism compares the two composites of (4.5.7) using compatibility of the Künneth maps with base change (VS7/fine-six-functor-identities), compatibility of κ_{U/T} with composition of smooth maps U″ → U′ → T (VS11/modified-kunneth-map, comp), and the identification K_{U″/T} ≅ K_{U″/U′} ⊗ K_{U′/T}.
Monoidality: (X₁ ×_T X₂) ×_S (X′₁ ×_{T′} X′₂) ≅ (X₁ ×_S X′₁) ×_{T ×_S T′} (X₂ ×_S X′₂), with the sheaves matched by the symmetric monoidal structure of ⊠ and B^{-1} ⊠ B′^{-1} = (B ⊠ B′)^{-1}.
Coherence (associativity of the 2-isomorphisms) reduces to the coherence of base change isomorphisms in the enhanced operation map (VS7/fine-shriek-functors).
The source states these as straightforward but tedious and omits them; they are planned here as proof obligations.
acceptance: For trivial bases the statement is the functoriality of the tensor product of CoCorr_S.
Applied to coev and ev of dualizable objects with common base it gives the dualizability of 𝔛₁ ⊠_𝔗 𝔛₂ (VS11/kunneth-for-characteristic-classes).

nodes.title: A Künneth formula for characteristic classes
nodes.statement: Let T be a decent S-v-stack with π : T → S and Δ_{T/S} cohomologically smooth, X₁, X₂ → T fine, and A_i ∈ D_ét(X_i, Λ) ULA over S. Then A₁ ⊠_T A₂ is ULA over S, In_S(X₁ ×_T X₂) ≅ In_S(X₁) ×_{In_S(T)} In_S(X₂), and cc_{X₁/S}(A₁) ⊠_{In_S(T)} cc_{X₂/S}(A₂) = cc_{X₁×_TX₂/S}(A₁ ⊠_T A₂), where ⊠_{In_S(T)} is the Künneth pairing (4.5.2) built from κ_{In_S(T)/S} and the trivialisation of VS11/smooth-base-dualizing-trivialization.
hypotheses: S is a decent v-stack; Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
π and Δ_{T/S} are cohomologically smooth; A_i is ULA over S.
proofSteps: Set 𝔛_i = (X_i → T, A_i, Λ_T) in BCoCorr_S; each is dualizable with dual (X_i → T, 𝔻_{X_i/S}A_i, K_{T/S}), the base (T, Λ_T) being dualizable by VS11/smooth-base-dualizing-trivialization.

𝔛 = 𝔛₁ ⊠_𝔗 𝔛₂ is dualizable with coev and ev obtained from those of 𝔛₁, 𝔗, 𝔛₂ through the monoidality isomorphism (VS11/based-fibre-product-coherence); hence 𝔖(𝔛) = (X₁ ×_T X₂, A₁ ⊠_T A₂) is dualizable, i.e. ULA (VS9/dualizable-iff-ula).

The functoriality 2-isomorphism identifies tr(1_𝔛) with tr(1_{𝔛₁}) ⊠_{tr(1_𝔗)} tr(1_{𝔛₂}); unwinding (4.5.7) the section is the image of cc(A₁) ⊗ cc(A₂) under κ_{In_S(T)/S} followed by the inverse of cc_{T/S}(Λ_T) (HKW22 proof of Theorem 4.5.3, with the misprint In_S(T₁) corrected to In_S(T)).
acceptance: For T = S, cc_{X₁/S}(A₁) ⊠_S cc_{X₂/S}(A₂) = cc_{X₁×_SX₂/S}(A₁ ⊠_S A₂), the analogue of tr(A ⊗ B) = tr(A)tr(B).
For X₁ = X₂ = T and A_i = Λ, both sides are cc_{T/S}(Λ_T).

nodes.title: The inertia stack of a quotient stack
nodes.statement: Let X be a nice diamond over S with an action α : X ×_S G → X of a cohomologically smooth S-group diamond G, and Y = [X/G]. For the correspondence c = (pr_X, α) : X ×_S G → X ×_S X, Fix(c) = {(x, g) : g(x) = x} is G-stable for h·(x, g) = (h(x), hgh^{-1}) and In_S(Y) ≅ [Fix(c)/G]; the map In_S(Y) → In_S([S/G]) ≅ [G//G] is the quotient of the projection Fix(c) → G, and the square Fix(c̃) → G over In_S(Y) → [G//G] is Cartesian, where c̃ = (id, α̃) on X_G = X ×_S G over G, α̃(x, g) = (g(x), g), Fix(c̃) ≅ Fix(c), and the fibre of Fix(c̃) over g ∈ G(S) is Fix(g).

X is a nice diamond over S; G is a cohomologically smooth S-group diamond acting on X.

Unwind In_S(Y) = Y ×_{Y ×_S Y} Y on the G-torsor X → Y, as for classifying stacks (VS11/inertia-of-classifying-stack).
Fix(c̃) is the fibre product of the graph of α̃ with the diagonal of X_G over G, which is Fix(c).

nodes.title: The universal local term of a group action
nodes.statement: For A ∈ D_ét([X/G], Λ) ULA over S, A_{X_G} = A|_{X_G} is ULA over G, and the G-equivariance of A gives ũ : A_{X_G} → α̃^*A_{X_G} = α̃^!A_{X_G} (α̃ is an isomorphism), so (c̃, ũ) is an endomorphism of the dualizable object (X_G, A_{X_G}) of CoCorr_G. Its trace tr_{c̃}(ũ, A_{X_G}) ∈ H^0(Fix(c̃), K_{Fix(c̃)/G}) is the universal local term: for every g ∈ G(S), restriction along g carries it to tr(g, u_g) ∈ H^0(Fix(g), K_{Fix(g)/S}), where u_g : A_X → g^*A_X is the equivariance isomorphism at g.
hypotheses: S is a decent v-stack; Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
X, G as in VS11/inertia-of-quotient-stack; A is ULA over S.
proofSteps: A_X is ULA over S because G → S is smooth (parent VS1/ula-descent-and-smooth-locality); A_{X_G} is ULA over G by base change.
α̃ is an automorphism of X_G over G, so α̃^* ≅ α̃^! and (c̃, ũ) is a 1-morphism of CoCorr_G; this is why one works over the base G (HKW22 p. 41).
Restriction to g ∈ G(S) is the base change of cohomological correspondences along g : S → G (VS10/base-change-of-cohomological-correspondences), which preserves traces.
acceptance: For G finite acting on a finite set X, the universal local term is the function (x, g) ↦ tr(u_g | A_x) on {g(x) = x}.
For g = 1, the restriction is cc_{X/S}(A_X).

nodes.statement: With notation as above, let ι : H^0(In_S(Y), K_{In_S(Y)/S}) → H^0(Fix(c̃), K_{Fix(c̃)/G}) be the composite of the isomorphism K_{In_S(Y)/[G//G]} ≅ p^!Λ ≅ p^!K_{[G//G]/S} ≅ K_{In_S(Y)/S} (from the trivialisation of VS11/smooth-base-dualizing-trivialization for T = [S/G]) with the pullback (4.6.1) along the Cartesian square of VS11/inertia-of-quotient-stack. Then ι(cc_{Y/S}(A)) = tr_{c̃}(ũ, A_{X_G}).

X, G, A as in VS11/universal-local-term.

tr_G = ev_G ∘ α₀ ∘ coev_G is an endomorphism of 𝔊 over tr(id_T) whose middle map sends g to its conjugacy class.

The functoriality of ⊠ (VS11/based-fibre-product-coherence) gives a 2-isomorphism 𝔖(cc_{Y/S}(A) ⊠_{cc_{[S/G]/S}(Λ)} tr_G(α₀)) ≅ F(tr(α)), F : CoCorr_G → CoCorr_S forgetting the base (HKW22 (4.6.4)); on sections this is the claimed equality (HKW22 proof of Theorem 4.6.1).

nodes.title: On an étale locus of fixed points the characteristic class is the local-term function
nodes.statement: Let U ⊂ G be an open conjugation-invariant subset and In_S([X/G])_U the preimage of [U//G]. Assume Fix(c̃)_U → U is étale (for instance, the fixed points vary locally constantly over U, as for strongly regular elements acting on affine Grassmannians). Then In_S([X/G])_U → [U//G] is étale, K_{In_S([X/G])_U/S} ≅ Λ canonically, and cc_{[X/G]/S}(A) restricted over U is the continuous function (x, g) ↦ loc_x(g, A) on {(x, g) ∈ X ×_S U : g(x) = x}.
hypotheses: S is a decent v-stack; Λ is a commutative ring with nΛ = 0 for an integer n prime to p.
X, G, A as in VS11/universal-local-term; U ⊂ G open and conjugation invariant; Fix(c̃)_U → U is étale.
The étaleness hypothesis replaces the source's assumption that elements of U have only isolated fixed points, which does not imply it (sourceIssues).
proofSteps: Étaleness descends along the smooth surjection U → [U//G] from the Cartesian square of VS11/inertia-of-quotient-stack.
K_{[U//G]/S} ≅ Λ canonically by VS11/smooth-base-dualizing-trivialization (restricted to the open [U//G] by VS9/characteristic-class-open-restriction), and étale pullback preserves it.

By VS11/characteristic-class-of-quotient-is-universal-local-term and VS11/universal-local-term, the restriction at g ∈ U(S) is tr(g, u_g), whose value at an isolated fixed point x is loc_x(g, A) (VS10/local-terms).
acceptance: For G a smooth group acting on P¹ with U the hyperbolic elements (two distinct fixed points), the function is identically 1 for A = Λ.

Counterexample to the source's hypothesis: for the smooth group of matrices [[a, b], [0, 1]] (a ∈ 1 + pO, b ∈ O) over C acting on P¹ and U = G ∖ {1}, every element of U has isolated fixed points, but the reduced fixed locus over U is two sections meeting along a = 1, not étale over U.

gaps.title: Are proper fine maps of decent v-stacks representable?
gaps.detail: Hansen–Kaletha–Weinstein Theorem 4.1.8 asserts Rf_! ≅ Rf_* for every proper fine map of decent v-stacks. Proper maps are 0-truncated (Scholze Definitions 10.7, 18.1), but it is not established that a proper fine map is representable in locally spatial diamonds: 0-truncated decent v-sheaves need not be diamonds (Spd Z_p), Scholze Proposition 13.4(v) reduces local spatiality to representability in diamonds plus quasiseparatedness, and Gulotta–Hansen–Weinstein Proposition 4.3(i) leaves the related representability claim as an exercise. The plan therefore takes proper 2-morphisms and proper pushforwards to be proper nice (proper and representable in locally spatial diamonds), which covers every use in Hansen–Kaletha–Weinstein; extending VS6–VS10 to all proper fine maps needs this representability.
